rationale: Neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphic facies, brain anomalies, and seizures (OMIM #621201), caused by biallelic GTF3C3 variants, consistently presents with structural brain anomalies (HP:0000707). Multiple independent cohorts document corpus callosum hypoplasia/dysgenesis (HP:0002079), delayed myelination (HP:0002188), and cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy across the majority of imaged individuals (e.g., De Hayr et al., 2025; Papuc et al., 2019; Chapleau et al., 2026). While some cohorts emphasize cerebellar atrophy and frontal lobe hypoplasia (Abdel-Hamid et al., 2025), structural neuroimaging defects—particularly involving white matter tracts, the corpus callosum, and the cerebellum—remain core diagnostic hallmarks.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 affected individuals from 7 unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants, patients presented with intellectual disability, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.

evidence.text: Four patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants showed brain imaging with brain atrophy, predominant cerebellar involvement, hypoplasia of the frontal lobes, and simplified gyral pattern in one patient, with seizures observed in 2 of 4 individuals.

source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern. Seizures were observed in half of the patients.

conflicts: While callosal hypoplasia and delayed myelination are highlighted in several reports, some cohorts emphasize cerebellar atrophy and frontal lobe hypoplasia over corpus callosum agenesis/hypoplasia, suggesting cerebellar involvement is an equally prominent hallmark.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of corpus callosum hypoplasia versus cerebellar atrophy across all centrally reviewed MRI scans of GTF3C3 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in radiologist interpretation across independent cohorts (e.g., De Hayr et al. vs Abdel-Hamid et al.) suggest that a centralized blind neuroimaging re-review is needed to determine which specific white matter or infratentorial structural anomaly is most sensitive.

new_directions.question_text: Does the severity of delayed myelination or corpus callosum hypoplasia correlate with residual RNA polymerase III transcription levels in GTF3C3 patient cells?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether hypomorphic missense variants cause milder myelination delays compared to truncating or splice-altering variants will aid genotype-phenotype differentiation.
